committee: CC Resident Services and Public Engagement Committee
overview: The Resident Services and Public Engagement Committee manages the City Council's communication strategies and public outreach initiatives to improve resident access to municipal government. Its work consistently centers on the production of a regular council newsletter and the facilitation of direct engagement through listening sessions and neighborhood meetings. Over the 2024-2025 and 2026-2027 terms, the committee has also reviewed major ordinance updates regarding human rights, immigration policy, and noise regulations. At its most recent meetings, the committee has focused on executing a city-wide tour of neighborhood ward meetings and auditing the city website for accessibility and accuracy.

threads.name: City Council Newsletter
threads.summary: The committee maintains a recurring process for drafting, editing, and approving the City Council newsletter to summarize legislative actions for the public. Initially, drafts were approved meeting-by-meeting with specific content updates on items like tax deferrals or school solar projects. By early 2026, the committee shifted to a monthly rotation where individual councilors author the draft, and later proposed a resolution to approve the newsletter independently of the full council.

threads.name: Neighborhood Ward Meetings and Outreach
threads.summary: Beginning with informal listening sessions at the Senior Center and public library, the committee worked to reach residents who do not traditionally attend council meetings. This effort evolved into a formal plan to hold hybrid meetings in each of the city's eight wards over a two-year period to discuss local concerns. As of late 2026, the committee is coordinating the schedule for these meetings through February 2027, following an inaugural session in Ward 1.

threads.name: Human Rights Commission Modernization
threads.summary: The committee reviewed and updated the enabling ordinance for the Human Rights Commission to modernize its operations. Key discussions included membership size, officer roles, and the establishment of member stipends. The final proposal, which set membership at 11 individuals with an annual stipend of $1,250, was referred to the full City Council in May 2025.

threads.name: Noise Ordinance Update
threads.summary: In late 2026, the committee began reviewing a proposal to update the city's 1974 noise ordinance, citing challenges with current enforcement. Councilor Tseng presented a draft based on a peer municipality's model that utilizes measurable decibel limits and a non-criminal fine structure. The matter remains in committee pending a public survey and consultation with the police department and local businesses.

threads.name: FY 2026 Budget Public Engagement
threads.summary: To increase transparency in the municipal budget process, the committee developed a public feedback survey. The committee refined the survey to include budget visualizations and demographic questions to better understand resident priorities. Results from 110 respondents identified schools, infrastructure, and housing as primary concerns, and the final report was distributed to the full council in mid-2025.

threads.name: Welcoming City Ordinance
threads.summary: The committee held a public hearing on the Welcoming City Ordinance, which codifies non-cooperation with federal immigration authorities on non-criminal matters. After a period of public comment involving residents and advocacy groups, the committee recommended the ordinance for adoption with minor technical amendments.

threads.name: City Website Improvements
threads.summary: The committee initiated a review of the municipal website, MedfordMass.org, following an audit that highlighted broken links and outdated content. A tiered improvement plan was proposed to address both quick content fixes and long-term structural changes. The committee plans to coordinate further with the IT and Communications departments to implement these accessibility and navigation updates.
